argument_markdown:
## Source-backed inputs

The sole DAG dependency is ATT-0112, and every one of its claims was independently confirmed by REV-0157 and REV-0158. We use CLM-0112-2, CLM-0112-6, CLM-0112-7 and CLM-0112-8: H^bal is smooth of pure dimension 18; Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2] is smooth of pure dimension 15; every component meets type (i); and on a qualifying scheme atlas the ordering monodromy is S_6. No Tate conclusion is imported from that dependency.

The packet supplies the balanced-family facts h^0(L_s)=3, base-point-freeness of L_s, nonemptiness of the distinct-support open, rational finite-quotient transfer, the right-coset convention, the incidence presentation D_univ=P_{C_univ}(G), and the corner-weight localization lemma. These are FND-0130, FND-0134, FND-0139, FND-0142, FND-0151, FND-0152, FND-0155, FND-0165, FND-0166 and FND-0167.

## Proof

Let V be as stated. Since Hbar^bal is smooth of pure dimension 15 by ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7, V is a smooth 15-dimensional scheme. A connected regular scheme has disjoint irreducible components, hence V is normal and integral.

Pull back H^bal->Hbar^bal along V and call the resulting PGL_2-torsor V_tilde->V. Its fibres are geometrically connected and V is connected, so V_tilde is connected. The map V_tilde->H^bal is etale onto an open substack. By ATT-0112/CLM-0112-6 this open meets the dense type-(i) locus. FND-0155 and ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 therefore give full S_6 monodromy for the ordering torsor after pullback to V_tilde. The monodromy over U contains the image after any base change, so its image is already S_6.

The balanced fibre calculations give h^0(L_s)=3 and base-point-freeness for every s. Grauert applies because V is reduced, so pi_*L is locally free of rank three and A=P_V(pi_*L) is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle. The distinct-support locus U is a nonempty dense open in every fibre. Thus A and U are normal integral of dimension 15+2=17. The right S_6-torsor Z->U has degree 6!=720. For a right torsor its connected components are indexed by the orbit set H\S_6 for left multiplication, so H=S_6 gives one component; this is the full-image criterion, not mere transitivity on six letters. Since Z is finite etale over normal U, it is normal, and connected normal Z is irreducible. This proves clause (1).

For clause (2), rational transfer for the free finite quotients gives

Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q)^{S_6}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U;Q)

and

Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q)^{S_5}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z^(1);Q).

Let Y=A\U with its reduced structure. Compact-support localization contains H_c^15(Y)->H_c^16(U)->H_c^16(A). Deligne's bound gives weights at most 15 on H_c^15(Y); strictness of the weight filtration therefore makes Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U)->Gr^W_16 H_c^16(A) injective. The compact-support projective-bundle formula for A->V yields

Gr^W_16 H_c^16(A)=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(V) direct-sum Gr^W_14 H_c^14(V)(-1) direct-sum Gr^W_12 H_c^12(V)(-2),

which is the first injection.

Base-point-freeness gives h^0(L_s(-p))=2 for every p in C_s. Grauert therefore makes G=pr_{2*}(pr_1^*L(-diagonal)) locally free of rank two, and the incidence divisor is D_univ=P_{C_univ}(G), a Zariski-locally trivial P^1-bundle. Its reduced-support open is Z^(1)=D_univ x_A U=Z/S_5. Applying the same localization argument to Z^(1) inside D_univ and then the P^1-bundle formula gives the second injection.

If E=direct-sum_rho V_rho tensor M_rho, rational Frobenius reciprocity and Ind_{S_5}^{S_6}(1)=[6] direct-sum [5,1] give E^{S_5}=M_[6] direct-sum M_[5,1]. This representation-theoretic identity identifies multiplicity spaces only; it does not create Tate structure.

Under (H-S), every summand on the right of the first injection is a sum of Q(-8), because Q(-7)(-1)=Q(-6)(-2)=Q(-8). Under (H-C), the same is true on the right of the second injection. Pure polarizable rational Hodge structures are semisimple, so the corresponding subobjects are sums of Q(-8). Duality between Gr^W_16 H_c^16 and T_16 changes Q(-8) to Q(8), proving clause (3).

## Computational hypotheses and gaps

No finite computation or experiment is used. The proof does not establish (H-S), (H-C), any remaining S_6-isotypic multiplicity, or any map or support-exhaustion statement in M_{6,6}. These are the explicit gaps below, so RED-0001 is not concluded.

claims.statement: For every connected component V of a separated finite-type etale scheme atlas of Hbar^bal, V is smooth normal integral of dimension 15, the balanced reduced-support ordering model Z has pure dimension 17, its ordering monodromy image is S_6, and Z->U is connected irreducible finite etale of degree 720.

With Q-coefficients, Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z)^{S_6}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U), while Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z)^{S_5}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z^(1))=M_[6] direct-sum M_[5,1] for the multiplicity Hodge structures in the rational S_6-isotypic decomposition.

The S_6-invariant weight-16 corner injects into the degree 16, 14 and 12 constant-coefficient corners of V with twists 0, -1 and -2, and the S_5-invariant corner injects into the degree 16 and 14 constant-coefficient corners of C_univ with twists 0 and -1.

The explicitly stated hypothesis (H-S) implies that T_16(Z)^{S_6}=T_16(U) is a sum of Q(8), and the explicitly stated hypothesis (H-C) implies that the [6]- and [5,1]-isotypic components of T_16(Z) are sums of Q(8).

gap_markers.statement: Prove that Gr^W_{2j}H_c^{2j}(V;Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(-j) for j=6,7,8.
Prove that Gr^W_16 H_c^16(C_univ;Q) and Gr^W_14 H_c^14(C_univ;Q) have Tate types Q(-8) and Q(-7), respectively.
Control every S_6-isotypic multiplicity of Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q) other than [6] and [5,1]; rational representation theory alone does not constrain its Hodge type.

Construct and verify the required closed support in M_{6,6}, the stack-level comparison or singleton-fibre recovery, the Gysin degree shift, and support exhaustion before identifying T_16(Z) with the exact RED-0001 contribution.
Nonreduced bases, stack-inertia component formulas, integral coefficients and coarse-moduli descent require separate arguments.

novelty_claims: Combines the dual-confirmed absence of purely type-(ii) balanced components with the PGL_2 quotient to make full S_6 monodromy automatic on every connected 15-dimensional etale atlas chart, yielding a connected irreducible 17-dimensional ordered model before applying the established constant-coefficient corner comparisons.

summary: On every 15-dimensional scheme atlas chart of the balanced PGL_2-quotient, the dual-confirmed component theorem ATT-0112 makes the type-(i) monodromy hypothesis automatic. The resulting 17-dimensional ordered model is connected and irreducible with full S_6 monodromy. Compact-support localization and the P^2/P^1 projective-bundle formulas then place the exact weight-16 trivial and standard representation corners inside constant-coefficient weight corners of the balanced base and its universal curve. This proves precise conditional Tate criteria but does not prove those base corners Tate, control the remaining S_6-isotypics, or assemble a supported contribution in M_{6,6}.

theorem_statement: Theorem (balanced-quotient atlas corner lemma). Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2], and let V be a connected component of a separated finite-type etale scheme atlas of Hbar^bal. Pull back the universal balanced tetragonal (CE)+(N) family pi:C_univ->V and its degree-six residual line bundle L. Put A=P_V(pi_*L), let U be the distinct-support open, let Z=Ord(U)->U be the finite etale right S_6-torsor of orderings, let D_univ be the universal divisor in C_univ x_V A, and put Z^(1)=D_univ x_A U=Z/S_5. Then: (1) V is smooth, normal and integral of dimension 15; A, U and Z have pure dimension 17. The ordering monodromy over U is S_6, so Z->U is connected of degree 720 and Z is irreducible. (2) Writing E=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q), there are canonical injections of pure weight-sixteen Hodge structures E^{S_6}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U;Q) -> Gr^W_16 H_c^16(V;Q) direct-sum Gr^W_14 H_c^14(V;Q)(-1) direct-sum Gr^W_12 H_c^12(V;Q)(-2), and E^{S_5}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z^(1);Q) -> Gr^W_16 H_c^16(C_univ;Q) direct-sum Gr^W_14 H_c^14(C_univ;Q)(-1). If E=direct-sum_rho V_rho tensor M_rho is its rational S_6-isotypic decomposition, then E^{S_5}=M_[6] direct-sum M_[5,1]. (3) Consequently, hypothesis (H-S), that Gr^W_{2j}H_c^{2j}(V;Q) is a sum of Q(-j) for j=6,7,8, implies T_16(Z)^{S_6}=T_16(U) is a sum of Q(8); hypothesis (H-C), that Gr^W_16 H_c^16(C_univ;Q) is a sum of Q(-8) and Gr^W_14 H_c^14(C_univ;Q) is a sum of Q(-7), implies that the [6]- and [5,1]-isotypic components of T_16(Z)=W_{-16}H_16^{BM}(Z;Q) are sums of Q(8). Neither (H-S) nor (H-C) is asserted here.
